thread:
Alex Kim: hitting a weird 429 pattern for a customer, need help scoping. they say they used a project-scoped API key but traffic is being throttled by org-level quota instead.
Maya Patel: can you paste the exact error body? 429s include scope normally.
Alex Kim: here — received from our logs: `{\n  \"error\": \"rate_limited\",\n  \"status\": 429,\n  \"detail\": \"quota exceeded\",\n  \"scope\": \"org\"\n}`
Alex Kim: customer insists they hit per-key limits not org. they have 3 projects under same org.
Liam Chen: quick checklist: are they sending an Authorization header with the key, or using an org token? also any proxy/fronting that might strip Authorization?
Alex Kim: they send auth header. but they also route through a legacy proxy that does connection pooling.
Sophie Lopez: connection pooling can collapse many logical client IPs into one source IP — if we apply IP-based burst caps that could explain it.
Maya Patel: do we apply IP throttles *in addition* to key/org quotas?
Liam Chen: yes, there's an IP throttle layer for anonymous or unkeyed requests + an extra soft burst cap globally to avoid spikes. 
Liam Chen: policy order is roughly: 1) project key quota 2) org quota 3) IP-based protections 4) global burst cap fallback. the 429 `scope` field should reflect which enforced rule fired — returns `scope: ip` or `scope: project` usually.
Alex Kim: but logs show `scope: org` as above. they say only one project is high volume, other projects idle.
Sophie Lopez: possible causes: (a) their API key actually maps to the org-level bucket due to legacy mapping bug, (b) their key was rotated and requests hit a fallback org token, (c) internal bug where project id header missing -> default to org.
Maya Patel: how do we confirm the mapping? any admin API to introspect quotas per key?
Liam Chen: yes — support helper endpoints (internal) — `GET /internal/keys/{key_id}/quota` returns assigned scope. I can't share full output here, but can run it if you give me trace id.
Alex Kim: trace id from their last failed request: `tr_20260315_7a9b` (I redacted actual key).
Liam Chen: running lookup... infra-bot: ran key lookup for trace tr_20260315_7a9b -> mapped_scope: project, project_id: proj-42, org_id: org-99, last_seen_proxy: proxy-1.internal.
Liam Chen: so key is mapped to project. the 429 scope=org suggests the org-wide pool is depleted. that can happen if other projects under org consumed quota.
Sophie Lopez: customer said other projects idle — did they have warmup or bursts earlier? quota windows can be consumed by scheduled jobs. check Billing/Usage UI for org-99.
Alex Kim: customer provided screenshot showing credits available at org level. but maybe they hit a rate (requests/sec) cap not credits.
Maya Patel: good point. we have two axes: budget/credits (token units) and steady-state RPS SLO. 429s can be from either. error body should include reason but often it's generic.
Liam Chen: also check if requests came with `X-Forwarded-For` now: proxy-1.internal sets XFF to client IP; if proxy didn't forward original client IP but rewrote with its own, our IP bucket will attribute to proxy IP which can push to org-level triggers earlier.
Alex Kim: customer logs show their backend used keepalive, no X-Forwarded-For set, so proxy IP is the egress.
Sophie Lopez: that favors IP-based collapse theory. but still doesn't explain why scope=org was returned.
Liam Chen: internal note: when org budget exhausted we return scope=org even if the immediate throttle was an interplay of IP burst and org fallback. edge case where two limits race: IP soft cap blocks some tokens then org bucket gets drained trying to retry.
Maya Patel: recommended next steps I tell the customer: 1) Confirm their key id in the failing request (redact) 2) Have them test a single direct request bypassing proxy (curl from a laptop) to see if Authorization still honored and scope changes.
Maya Patel: provide curl snippet:
```\ncurl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-REDACTED\" \\\n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n  -d '{"input": "test"}' \\\n  https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/generate\n```
Maya Patel: and one emulating proxied requests (no X-Forwarded-For):
```\ncurl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-REDACTED\" \\\n  -H \"X-Forwarded-For: 10.0.0.1\" \\\n  -d '{"input":"test"}' https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/generate\n```
Alex Kim: ran the direct test from their laptop — success, no 429s. proxied test returns 429 with `scope: org`.
Liam Chen: that nails it: proxy egress IP or header behavior causing our protective logic to treat traffic as coming from same source; org global budget got hit because several projects behind same proxy spiked.
Sophie Lopez: what mitigation can we offer?
Liam Chen: options: - Short term: instruct customer to set X-Org-ID or X-Project-ID header (we accept these for routing) and update proxy to forward original client IP as X-Forwarded-For. - Mid term: we can add an allowlist for their proxy IP (if they own it) to exempt from IP burst rules while still counting against project quotas. - Longer term: engineering can tweak mapping so project tokens always take precedence over org fallback when Authorization present.
Maya Patel: we should escalate for policy change. can you open an eng ticket with repro steps and traces? tag eng-runtime. include trace tr_20260315_7a9b, proxy-1.internal egress, and sample curl.
Alex Kim: opening ticket now. description: \"Auth+proxy interactions causing org-level 429; direct requests succeed; proxied requests 429 scope=org; probable attribution collapse to proxy IP; requesting mapping fix and docs update.\"
Alex Kim: added logs, traces, and customer's permission to share redacted traces.
infra-bot: created ENG-1234 in eng-runtime: \"auth-proxy-ip-attribution-org-throttle\" assigned to Liam Chen.
Liam Chen: I'll take the bug. immediate support reply to customer: ask them to forward proxy config and whether they can set X-Project-ID header or forward original client IP. also offer a temporary proxy IP allowlist if they confirm ownership.
Sophie Lopez: also note billing impact: if org quota consumed, they may see unexpected billing or token rejections. clarify that allowlist doesn't change token accounting, just the protective IP layer.
Maya Patel: I'll message the customer with those steps and link to ENG-1234.
Alex Kim: thanks team. leaving thread open for when eng has a fix or policy change. :thumbsup:
